before.title: Pending tab: one collapsed row per build (rebuild)
before.detail: Rebuild from current main (the old branch claude/pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-build is 3000+ commits behind and only has rename commits; ignore it). In the Build Orchestrator's Pending tab, every pending build is ONE collapsed row: title, status/why it's pending, priority, steps done/total, age. Tap the row to expand it and see steps, notes and actions (queue, edit, archive); tap again to collapse. Collapsed by default, remembers expanded rows per viewer. Same for desktop and phone. Uses asset tokens and framework controls; full API parity (deep link, expand/collapse and actions via REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Tests, help, Shipped features. Land when done.

notes.text: Brett: every grid is supposed to be 1 or 2 rows per item depending on the skin. So the collapsed row height (one-line vs two-line) comes from the active skin's grid tokens, not hard-coded.
Split by Claude into 14 steps (0 Fable).
Claude account: mossesx-max- (mossesx@gmail.com) (axf-pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-2--paulie, shared account login)

Brett (06:55): for the CURRENT skin (the console default), the Pending tab uses the 2-row layout, packed with info, buttons and badges. Row 1: title, priority, status badge, action buttons (queue, land, edit, archive, open PR). Row 2: badges/info: commits behind main, date+time added, date+time built, PR #, steps done/total, account/model, why it's pending. Status badges: pending build, queued, building, built/waiting to merge, merging, landed, clashing, failed, held. ANIMATION: any build that's actively doing something (building, merging, splitting, landing) gets its icon/badge animated (e.g. a spinner or pulse) using the skin's animation tokens (#652); idle states stay still; respects reduced motion. Same badge set reused by the every-grid build so all grids can show it.

At: 2026-11-15T11:52:18.052Z
> Why are pending builds not 1 expandable row. Wanna just rebuild it

Brett said (2026-11-15 11:52):

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (14 left, ~2.2 h):
[ ] s1 (~8 min) Read the current Pending tab in the Build Orchestrator plugin from main. Map where pending rows are drawn, which data they read (status, why pending, priority, steps, age) and which actions exist (queue, edit, archive). Write the map as a short design note in the build report draft.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Add a pure helper, pending-rows.mjs. For one build it gives the collapsed-row summary: title, status label, why it is pending, priority, steps done/total and age. It also handles the expanded-set state per viewer: toggle, expand, collapse, collapse all and the storage key. Add unit tests for it.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Server: store expanded rows per viewer on the plugin data dir (key = viewer/session id). Add REST routes: GET pending/rows (summaries plus each row's expanded flag), POST pending/rows/<id>/expand|collapse|toggle and POST pending/rows/collapse-all.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Build a PendingRow component on framework controls only (TabGroup is not used; Container/Button/Chip/PriorityTag) with asset tokens. Collapsed by default, it shows one line: title, status chip with why it is pending, PriorityTag, steps done/total and age. It has a tap target with aria-expanded and a data-axf-target row:<build> address.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Expanded body of PendingRow: step list with done ticks and Fable/Opus badges, notes and What Brett said. It also has an actions toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label, settings id) with Queue, Edit and Archive wired to the existing orchestrator/pipeline calls. Archive keeps its confirm. Tap the header again to collapse.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Swap the Pending tab's old list for PendingRow rows. Load the expanded state from the GET route, write it back on toggle, and add a Collapse all button. Remove the old multi-row rendering and its dead CSS.
[ ] s7 (~8 min) Phone layout: the collapsed row wraps to two lines at narrow widths without overlap (title, then chips). The expanded actions stay tappable at tap-target size and use tokens only. Run check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets on the plugin and fix any findings.
[ ] s8 (~10 min) API part 1 (deep link and console control). Register control targets view:builds/tab:orchestrator=pending and row:<build> with expand/collapse/toggle actions. Make console_show/console_open on row:<build> open the Pending tab with that row expanded and highlighted. Add the deep link ?axf-target=row:<build>. Run check-console-control.
[ ] s9 (~10 min) API part 2 (MCP, CLI and voice). Add plugin commands pending-rows (list with state), pending-expand, pending-collapse, pending-toggle and pending-collapse-all. They are read statically from the routes for MCP. Add CLI subcommands in orchestrator.mjs (pending rows|expand|collapse|toggle|collapse-all) and AmberX voice actions. Queue, edit and archive reuse the existing commands; check they are listed.
[ ] s10 (~10 min) Parity test: one script calls REST, MCP command, CLI and voice action for list, expand, collapse and toggle on a fixture build. It asserts all four give the same state. Add server route tests for per-viewer separation (viewer A expanded does not expand for viewer B).
[ ] s11 (~8 min) Help and glossary: update the plugin help for the Pending tab (one row per build, tap to expand, remembered per viewer, API addresses). Add descriptions for the new commands. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check and the help ratchet.
[ ] s12 (~10 min) Shots and UI Review: build the console from the worktree (vite preview with mocked /api/me and hub data). Shoot desktop and phone views of the Pending tab: collapsed, one expanded and the phone expanded view. Submit with review.mjs submit with at least 3 choices (row density / chip layout options as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), group 'pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-2 - <time>'.
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Run the full checks: plugin tests, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check and builds-store verify. Confirm the Shipped features ledger got the feature rows from the build hook. Fix anything red.
[ ] s14 (~10 min) Write the report (_claude/builds/reports/pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-2.md): before/after, how each feature is reached (deep link, REST, MCP, CLI, voice), tests and UI Review item. Update the THREADS.md row. Push the branch and link it with builds-live.mjs link. Open the PR, saying it waits on UI Review and listing the API parity. Add it to the merge queue to land.
